author: K. L. Pryor
title: Grade 3 students lead math MCA participation at Dover-Eyota Elementary in 2024-25
text:
The Minnesota Department of Education reported that Dover-Eyota Elementary School’s third-graders recorded the highest participation rate in the mathematics part of the 2024-25 MCA.
Among the 248 students who completed that section of the exam at Dover-Eyota Elementary, 74 were in third grade.
Overall, 72% of third-grade test takers were deemed proficient in mathematics based on the exam’s criteria.
The MCA and the Alternate Minnesota Comprehensive Assessment (Alt MCA) serve as state exams to measure student achievement against Minnesota’s academic standards while also fulfilling federal and state requirements. These assessments evaluate math, reading, and science skills by grade level. Most students take the MCA; however, those in special education who qualify may opt for the Alt MCA instead.
According to Minnesota’s Report Card, statewide proficiency rates on the MCA exams have fallen since before the pandemic . For instance, math proficiency declined by more than 7% from 2019, and reading proficiency dropped by almost 5%.
